top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a new measurement principle: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the lattice light shift and removes Doppler and recoil effects while interrogating many atoms in parallel. It has been reproduced and surpassed independently, with comparisons agreeing near 10^-18, and it already serves as a precision tool for fundamental physics and geodesy. The allocation to Katori (invention and first realization) and Ye (realization at the 10^-18 level) is exact, and the citation is well scoped, so an award is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Possible mild connection: as a PhD student the member spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, the group tradition from which Jun Ye comes, and works in the same atomic-physics and laser-spectroscopy field. No direct collaboration or institutional tie to Katori or Ye is apparent from the profile.
